title: Token Shield integration contract v1
description: Shape of token-shield.integration.json, a declaration any optimization plugin may ship in its own installed plugin root. Every field read from a file matching this schema is labeled DECLARED by Token Shield discovery, never CURATED: a declaration is the plugin's own claim about itself, not a first-party verification. Enforced in code by discover_companions.py's _validate_declaration (standard library only, no jsonschema dependency); this file is the human-readable mirror of that same contract and is kept in agreement with it by hand. See docs/superpowers/specs/integration-contract-v1.md for the full contract, including the curated-plus-declaring collision rule.

capabilities.description: What the plugin does to token usage. Token Shield's own vocabulary (minimal_code, output_compression, tool_output_isolation, deterministic_deduplication) is recommended where it applies, but any non-empty string is accepted.

name.description: The plugin's own name. When it matches a name already curated in data/companions.json, the curated evidence wins and the collision is reported.

modes.description: Operating modes the plugin supports, for example off, lite, full.

status_command.description: How a user or tool checks whether the plugin is currently active.

version_command.description: How a user or tool checks the plugin's installed version.

activation_command.description: How a user turns the plugin on (install or enable).

rollback_command.description: How a user turns the plugin off or removes it. Declaring this does not grant curation; it lets Token Shield report it as DECLARED where curation would otherwise have blocked the plugin entirely for lacking documented evidence of this path.
